rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's composure and trust in God lead him to admit the killing and mention its eventual good outcome, though he had not foreseen that benefit.
rows.anchor: كانت رباطة جأش موسى وتوكله على ربه باعثة له على الاعتراف بالفعلة وذكر ما نشأ عنها من خير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He confesses first to show Pharaoh that the accusation has not affected or intimidated him.
rows.anchor: فابتدأ بالإقرار بفعلته ليعلم فرعون أنه لم يجد لكلامه مدخل تأثير في نفس موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses delays answering the reminder of his upbringing because he sees it as an attempt to stop him confronting Pharaoh with the Lord who sent him.
rows.anchor: لأنه علم أن القصد منه الإقصار من مواجهته بأن ربا أعلى من فرعون أرسل موسى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers the charge of the killing first because Pharaoh intends it to silence him; Moses shows no fear of a demand for blood, trusting God to protect him.
rows.anchor: لأنه علم أنه أدخل في قصد الإفحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here idhā is a particle of response and recompense; its final nūn is part of the word, not tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وكلمة { إذا } هنا حرف جواب وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing فعلتها before إذن makes the confession immediate and implies that Moses is unafraid to acknowledge it.
rows.anchor: وقدم { فعلتها } على ( إذن ) مبادرة بالإقرار ليكون كناية عن عدم خشيته من هذا الإقرار

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reads Pharaoh's charge as saying Moses repaid their upbringing with the killing; Moses answers in the same terms, conceding the wording and calling it fitting recompense.
rows.anchor: أن قول فرعون { فعلت فعلتك } ( الشعراء : 19 ) يتضمن معنى جازيت نعمتنا بما فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the al-Kashshāf explanation of Moses's جواب بالموجب the clearest interpretation offered.
rows.anchor: وهذا أظهر ما قيل في تفسير هذه الآية

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: An alternative parses إذا as a ظرف detached from annexation, opened for ease and frequent use, rather than as a conditional particle.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المحققين : { إذا } ظرف مقطوع عن الإضافة مؤثرا فيه الفتح على الكسر لخفته وكثرة الدوران

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī allows إذ to be opened when its annexed noun is omitted and replaced by tanwīn; here it means the time when Pharaoh raised Moses, so the old reproach has no force.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين } أي فعلتها إذ ربيتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this time-adverb reading, إذا attaches to فعلتها and the omitted annexed phrase is understood from the verb: Moses did it when Pharaoh raised him.
rows.anchor: فيكون متعلقا ب { فعلتها } مقطوعا عن الإضافة لفظا لدلالة العامل على المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Raḍī, and al-Damāmīnī adopt the time-adverb reading; al-Qazwīnī's discussion appears to favor it too.
rows.anchor: هو مختار ابن عطية والرضي في ( شرح الحاجبية ) والدماميني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الضالين means moral wrongdoing, Moses says anger made him overlook the sanctity of life, a norm shared across human custom even before a revealed law; his confession in 28:16 supports this reading.
rows.anchor: أن سورة الغضب أغفلته عن مراعاة حرمة النفس وإن لم يكن يومئذ شريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, الضالين means straying from the truth through ignorance, since no divine law was yet available; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares 93:7.
rows.anchor: أي كنت يومئذ على غير معرفة بالحق لعدم وجود شريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either reading admits the apparent fact but defeats Pharaoh's attempt to use it against Moses's divine mission; Moses answers the charge of disbelief by saying he was misguided, not an unbeliever then.
rows.anchor: وعلى كلا الوجهين فجواب موسى فيه اعتراف بظاهر التقرير وإبطال لما يستتبعه من جعله حجة لتكذيبه برسالته عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses counters Pharaoh's claim that he was among the unbelievers with الضالين, specifically denying that he was then a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قابل قول فرعون { وأنت من الكافرين } ( الشعراء : 19 ) بقوله : { وأنا من الضالين } إبطالا لأن يكون يومئذ كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The escape is followed by God correcting, teaching, guiding, and commissioning Moses; this is purposeful explanation, since a person's present state and final outcome matter more than his past.
rows.anchor: فليس ذلك من موسى مجرد إطناب بل لأنه يفيد معنى أن الإنسان ابن يومه لا ابن أمسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ففررت منكم means Moses began fleeing away from Pharaoh and his people, who caused his flight; an implicit noun makes it ‘from fear of you,’ and they had conspired to kill him.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ففررت منكم } أي فرارا مبتدئا منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حكما means wisdom and knowledge, here Moses's prophethood, beginning when God spoke to him.
rows.anchor: وأراد بها النبوءة وهي الدرجة الأولى حين كلمه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses became a messenger after God showed him the sign, chose him, and commanded him to go to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: أرسله بقوله : { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returns to Pharaoh's opening boast about raising him, rejects its status as a favor, and treats the demonstrative as referring to the favor Pharaoh claimed.
rows.anchor: ثم عاد إلى أول الكلام فكر على امتنانه عليه بالتربية فأبطله وأبى أن يسميه نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes أن عبدت an explanatory clause for تلك, strengthening the point while turning Pharaoh's intended boast against him, like the construction in 15:66.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك لزيادة تقرير المعنى مع ما فيه من قلب مقصود فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing puts أن عبدت in the accusative after an omitted preposition of cause: ‘because you enslaved the Children of Israel.’
rows.anchor: والتقدير : لأن عبدت بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading supplies an omitted interrogative hamza, making the line a question of repudiation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الكلام استفهام بحذف الهمزة وهو استفهام إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبد means ‘subjugated’ or ‘humiliated,’ as shown by the causative form أعبد and a line cited by language authorities as lexical evidence.
rows.anchor: حتام يعبدني قومي وقد كثرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three readings turn Pharaoh's supposed favor into a grievance: Moses was raised only because Pharaoh's persecution and infanticide drove his mother to place him in the river, where Pharaoh's wife found him.
rows.anchor: أن نعمة تربيته ما كانت إلا بسبب إذلال بني إسرائيل إذ أمر فرعون باستئصال أطفال بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Showing kindness to Moses while oppressing his people does not make Pharaoh's treatment a favor or create a debt of gratitude.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن الإحسان إليه مع الإساءة إلى قومه لا يزيد إحسانا ولا منة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When intimidation fails and Moses persists in his mission, Pharaoh shifts to asking what the Lord of the Worlds is, the sender Moses and Aaron named.
rows.anchor: لما لم يرج تهويله على موسى عليه السلام وعلم أنه غير مقلع عن دعوته تنفيذا لما أمره الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an names Pharaoh explicitly here, rather than continuing the usual ‘he said’ dialogue formula, to clarify the speaker after a gap.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن تلك الطريقة إلى إظهار اسمه لإيضاح صاحب هذه المقالة لبعد ما بين قوله هذا وقوله الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw links Pharaoh's question back to his earlier question across the intervening speech by Moses.
rows.anchor: والواو عاطفة هذا الاستفهام على الاستفهام الأول الذي وقع كلام موسى فاصلا بينه وبين ما عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما commonly asks for the identity or nature of what follows; a report about the Prophet's question to a delegation, ‘What are you?’, illustrates its use to identify a group.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks Moses to identify the being he called the Lord of the Worlds.
rows.anchor: ففرعون سأل موسى عليه السلام تبيين حقيقة هذا الذي وصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptian religion assigned different gods control over elements and kinds of beings, rather than affirming one God; multiple controllers conflict with unity of governance.
rows.anchor: كانت عقائد القبط تثبت آلهة متفرقة قد اقتسمت التصرف في عناصر هذا العالم وأجناس الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Lord of the Worlds startled Pharaoh because it implied one God and denied the divinity of Egypt's familiar gods.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع فرعون من كلام موسى إثبات رب العالمين قرع سمعه بما لم يألفه من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Egyptians treated Pharaoh as a god-appointed ruler representing the other gods' will, and he therefore claimed divinity; Ibn ʿĀshūr cites his boast about ruling Egypt.
rows.anchor: فهو مظهر الآلهة الأخرى في تدبير المملكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People often imagined their own land as the whole world; rulers displayed victories over nearby peoples and hid defeats, while propagandists reinforced this outlook, explaining Pharaoh's astonished, rejecting question.
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام مشوب بتعجب وإنكار على طريق الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking for clarification is a normal first move in disputation, which is why Pharaoh first asks about the sender's identity.
rows.anchor: ومن دقائق هذه المجادلة أن الاستفسار مقدم في المناظرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses defines the Lord by the heavens, earth, and everything between them: a formal definition through created attributes, the furthest human knowledge of God reaches by considering creation.
rows.anchor: ومرجع هذا البيان إلى أنه تعريف لحقيقة الرب بخصائصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf's first of three analyses, also chosen by al-Sakkākī, treats the question and answer as a question about a genus answered with a fully matching definition.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا مختار السكاكي في قانون الطلب

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf and al-Miftāḥ say Moses's answer points listeners to infer the one Creator by contemplating the heavens, earth, and what lies between them.
rows.anchor: وأشار صاحب ( الكشاف ) وصرح صاحب ( المفتاح ) بأن جواب موسى بما يبين حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘If you are certain’ means willing to seek certainty and truth without stubborn denial; certainty follows from recognizing the unique Creator of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: أي إن كنتم مستعدين للإيقان طالبين لمعرفة الحقائق غير مكابرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘you’ includes everyone present, making the invitation comprehensive and clarifying the speakers' intended meaning before anyone is held accountable for a statement.
rows.anchor: مراد به جميع حاضري مجلس فرعون

rows.speaker: سحنون
rows.claim: Sahnūn says a person whose words or actions entail unbelief must be confronted with that implication; if he understands and accepts it, he is treated as an apostate and given three days to repent.
rows.anchor: قال سحنون فيمن صدر منه قول أو فعل يستلزم كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turns from Moses and addresses his courtiers, asking in astonishment why they have not listened, as though they had not heard him.
rows.anchor: أعرض فرعون عن خطاب موسى واستثار نفوس الملأ من حوله وهم أهل مجلسه فاستفهمهم استفهام تعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He stirs the courtiers against Moses so that Moses's proof will not persuade them.
rows.anchor: فنزلهم منزلة من لم يستمعه تهييجا لنفوسهم كي لا تتمكن منهم حجة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied surprise at their listening and silence also conveys surprise at Moses's claim; Pharaoh considers monotheism so objectionable that it cannot pass without response.
rows.anchor: ومرجع التعجبين أن إثبات رب واحد لجميع المخلوقات منكر عند فرعون لأنه كان مشركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Pharaoh's address to the courtiers answers Moses implicitly, the Qur'an reports it in the conventional form used for dialogue, as if he were answering Moses directly.
rows.anchor: ولكون خطاب فرعون لمن حوله يتضمن جوابا عن كلام موسى حكي كلام فرعون بالصيغة التي اعتيدت في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's reply answers Pharaoh's astonishment at the courtiers' silence; because Pharaoh bypassed Moses to address them, Moses now speaks to them all.
rows.anchor: كلام موسى هذا في معرض الجواب عن تعجب فرعون من سكوت من حوله فلذلك كانت حكايته قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first proof, creation of the worlds, is the broadest evidence of God's unity; when it fails, Moses moves to the nearer evidence of their own creation and their ancestors' deaths.
rows.anchor: فنزل بهم إلى الاستدلال بأنفسهم وبآبائهم إذ أوجدهم الله بعد العدم ثم أعدم آباءهم بعد وجودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmic proof is general, while human origins and death are closer to immediate experience; the death of known ancestors disproves eternity and thus their divinity.
rows.anchor: فالاستدلال الأول يمتاز بالعموم ، والاستدلال الثاني يمتاز بالقرب من الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Your earliest ancestors’ includes ancient Pharaohs whom Egyptians ranked as gods and called sons of the sun, represented by the deity Amun-Ra.
rows.anchor: وشمل عموم الآباء بإضافته إلى الضمير وبوصفه بالأولين بعض من يزعمونهم في مرتبة الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb here means both creator and master, the latter by virtue of creating.
rows.anchor: والرب : الخالق والسيد بموجب الخالقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh becomes angry because Moses's claim strips revered ancestors of divinity; he dismisses an argument that contradicts what he treats as necessary reason as madness.
rows.anchor: احتد فرعون لما ذكر موسى ما يشمل آباءه المقدسين بذكر يخرجهم من صفة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his elite recognize human formation only through gradual birth and overlook the creative power in ordinary processes, wrongly treating familiar development as evidence of no maker.
rows.anchor: لأن فرعون وملأه يرون تكوين الآدمي بالتولد وهم لا يحسبون التكوين الدال على الخالقية إلا التكوين بالطفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their simple minds rank a chick's formation from an egg below thunder and silkworm formation above human birth; they therefore call the ordinary origins and deaths of people madness because they miss their finer details.
rows.anchor: فهم يحسبون تكوين الفرخ من البيضة أقل من تكوين الرعد ، وأن تكوين دودة القز أدل على الخالق من تكوين الآدمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh reinforces the accusation with two emphatic particles because Moses's conduct does not suggest madness, making the charge doubtful; he claims special knowledge of Moses that listeners lack.
rows.anchor: وأكد كلامه بحرفي التأكيد لأن حالة موسى لا تؤذن بجنونه فكان وصفه بالمجنون معرضا للشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Moses ‘the messenger’ is mockery, signaled by Pharaoh's accompanying claim that he is certainly insane.
rows.anchor: وقصد بإطلاق وصف الرسول على موسى التهكم به بقرينة رميه بالجنون المحقق عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying ‘your messenger’ distances Pharaoh from the audience and from the person being addressed, reinforcing his contempt.
rows.anchor: وأضاف الرسول إلى المخاطبين ربئا بنفسه عن أن يكون مقصودا بالخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause repeats ‘your messenger’ for emphasis and specifies the target to stir the audience not to trust Moses; Pharaoh is preparing resistance because Moses may have supporters in Egypt.
rows.anchor: وتنصيصا على المقصود لزيادة تهييج السامعين كيلا يتأثروا أو يتأثر بعضهم بصدق موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since they misunderstand ordinary creation and remain unconvinced, Moses switches to the undeniable spectacle of the sun's eastward rise and westward setting each day.
rows.anchor: انتقل موسى إلى ما لا قبل لهم بجحده ولا التباسه وهو التصرف العجيب المشاهد كل يوم مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's move parallels Abraham's argument against Nimrod: after the life-and-death proof was distorted, Abraham argued from sunrise, making Moses's proof ‘Abrahamic.’
rows.anchor: فانتقل إبراهيم إلى الاستدلال بطلوع الشمس فيما حكى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes المشرق والمغرب as the places of sunrise and sunset; ‘Lord’ then means creator of the daily order, stated concisely.
rows.anchor: والمشرق والمغرب يجوز أن يراد بهما مكان شروق الشمس ومكان غروبها في الأفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes them as verbal nouns, ‘rising and setting’; ‘what lies between’ covers the changing stages of day and night, all signs of a precisely ordered creation.
rows.anchor: أي رب الشروق والغروب ، فيكون المراد بالرب الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported interpretation ‘owner of the two directions’ weakens the argument from a great observable sign and does not fit the conclusion ‘if you reason.’
rows.anchor: وهذا التفسير يفيت مناسبة الكلام لمقام الاستدلال بعظيم ولا يلاقي التذييل الواقع بعده في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the geographical reading, east and west are the known ends of the earth, a conventional argument that all the earth belongs to God because no known ruler, including Pharaoh, controlled it all.
rows.anchor: وتانك الجهتان هما منتهى الأرض المعروفة للناس يومئذ فكأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘If you reason’ urges rational reflection so listeners can grasp the proof; it pointedly answers Pharaoh's charge that Moses is mad, challenging them to prove they are the rational ones.
rows.anchor: أي إن كنتم أنتم العقلاء ، أي فلا تكونوا أنتم المجانين

rows.speaker: أبو تمام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr illustrates the retort with Abū Tammām's comeback to two critics who asked why he says what is not understood: ‘Why do you not understand what is said?’
rows.anchor: لم لا تفهمان ما يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dramatic reversal in the fortunes of Moses's two sides exceeds ordinary political change, showing special divine action that supported the messenger and his people and broke his enemies; the episode also contains proofs of monotheism.
rows.anchor: وكانت هذه القصة آية لأنها دالة على أن ذلك الانقلاب العظيم في أحوال الفريقين الخارج عن معتاد تقلبات الدول والأمم دليل على أنه تصرف إلهي خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's repeated close to each proof, ‘in that is a sign,’ has already been explained in the opening discussion.
rows.anchor: ووجه تذييل كل استدلال من دلائل الوحدانية وصدق الرسل في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's story follows Moses's and precedes Noah's, against the usual order, because Abraham's idol-worshipping people resemble Arab polytheists in their deaf idols, ancestral imitation, and need for rational proof.
rows.anchor: وقدمت هنا على قصة نوح على خلاف المعتاد في ترتيب قصصهم في القرآن لشدة الشبه بين قوم إبراهيم وبين مشركي العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the peoples of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Lot, and Midian, Abraham's people were not struck by worldly punishment, resembling Quraysh in being granted respite.
rows.anchor: وفي أن قوم إبراهيم لم يسلط عليهم من عذاب الدنيا مثل ما سلط على قوم نوح وعلى عاد وثمود وقوم لوط وأهل مدين فأشبهوا قريشا في إمهالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missions of Muhammad and Abraham rest on human nature in thought and practice, belief and law; God gave humanity this nature to uphold and use.
rows.anchor: فإن الله ما جعل في خلق الإنسان هذه الفطرة ليضيعها ويهملها بل ليقيمها ويعملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing that even Moses's many signs failed to move Pharaoh's stubborn people, God presents Abraham's reasoning-based call as a model close to Muhammad's for those demanding signs before belief.
rows.anchor: أعقب ذلك بضرب المثل بدعوة إبراهيم المماثلة لدعوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في النداء على إعمال دليل النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘them’ in the command to recount the story refers to people understood from context, as with the opening's ‘lest they believe.’
rows.anchor: عائد إلى معلوم من السياق كما تقدم في قوله أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham apparently asks while the people are actively worshipping, as the present tense indicates; they take it as a real question and answer that they worship idols and remain devoted to them.
rows.anchor: كما هو مناسب الإتيان بالمضارع في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite أصناما carries honorific force: they esteem the idols and boast of them, unlike Abraham's deliberately belittling term أوثانا in 29:17.
rows.anchor: ولذا عدل عن تعريفها وهم يعلمون أن إبراهيم يعرفها ويعلم أنهم يعبدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeat نعبد despite its presence in Abraham's question to boast about worship, then add ‘we remain devoted’ to intensify their claim.
rows.anchor: فعدلوا عن سنة الجواب إلى تكرير الفعل الواقع في السؤال ابتهاجا بهذا الفعل وافتخارا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نظل implies devotion throughout the day; Ibn ʿĀshūr says they were Sabians who used idols as daytime symbols for planets, then worshipped the visible planets at night.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فهم كانوا صابئة يعبدون الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb عاكفين incorporates the sense of worshippers, which explains its construction with لام rather than على.
rows.anchor: فعدي إليه الفعل باللام دون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a lord is sought in need and expected to benefit or harm, Abraham asks whether the idols hear their calls or can help or hurt, exposing their lack of divinity.
rows.anchor: ولما كان شأن الرب أن يلجأ إليه في الحاجة وأن ينفع أو يضر ألقى إبراهيم عليهم استفهاما عن حال هذه الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters worship images in hope of benefit or to ward off harm; some also worshipped devils.
rows.anchor: وكانت الأمم الوثنية تعبد الوثن لرجاء نفعه أو لدفع ضره ولذلك عبد بعضهم الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In يسمعونكم, the object ‘you’ stands for ‘your prayers’ by ellipsis, as confirmed by ‘when you call.’
rows.anchor: ضمير المخاطبين توسعا بحذف مضاف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham opens the debate in order to leave the idolaters unable to prove that their images hear, benefit, or harm.
rows.anchor: وأراد إبراهيم فتح المجادلة ليعجزوا عن إثبات أنها تسمع وتنفع
